title: Lack of backup led to fatal police shooting
article: Ideally, two police officers should have been dispatched to a fatal robbery and hostage-taking at a downtown drug store nearly 18 months ago.

But in reality, Deputy Chief Rick Hansen told a fatality inquiry Monday, it was a rare situation in which an officer was forced to fatally shoot a knife-wielding offender and it was impossible to fully prepare for. "A situation can occur like this at any time, but it's not predictable," Hansen said.

Arthur George Provencal was holding a knife to the throat of a Shoppers Drug Mart employee in TD Square on Dec. 23, 2000, when Const. Julien Gagne warned him to drop the knife before firing one fatal shot.

"My gut feeling is if there were two officers there, things could have been different," Al Koenig, president of the Calgary Police Association, said outside court Monday. "The only option Gagne had under these circumstances was to shoot."
Koenig said the issue of how many officers are in a vehicle has become part of the union's bargaining process.

Hansen said although two officers may have been beneficial in this instance, policy should not be unilaterally changed to make all units double-manned, as 84 per cent of all the Calgary Police Service's 250,000 annual calls require only one officer.
Provincial court Judge Heather Lamoureux said her report on the fatality inquiry will be available July 31.
